current_activity: delayed 51st Highland Division attack from the Orne bridgehead, contained by 21st Panzer; bridgehead also under attack
notes: I Corps' planned eastern thrust (51st (Highland) Division and 4th Armoured Brigade crossing into the 6th Airborne Division's Orne bridgehead, toward Cagny south-east of Caen) was postponed to 12 June because bad weather delayed the landing of the 51st Division and 4th Armoured Brigade (Wikipedia, Operation Perch, citing Ellis). The corps' own attack on 12 June was limited: the bridgehead was itself attacked all day from the Bréville area (346th Infantry Division per the Battle of Bréville page; the 21st Panzer Division was also opposing from the south), the Germans pulled back in the evening, and 12th Parachute Battalion and a Devonshire company captured Bréville that night. The 51st Division, opposed by 21st Panzer in its push south toward Sainte-Honorine, was contained, and the offensive east of Caen was called off on 13 June. The fighting was done by divisions (51st Highland, 6th Airborne), not by the corps headquarters; the point is a representative bridgehead point (Bréville-les-Monts commune coordinates), not the corps HQ.
